title: BenchMesh: per-route/model/region latency slices and heatmap portal
creator: Ava Chen
description: Deliver a new benchmarking and visualization pipeline (BenchMesh) that captures p95/p99 and tokens/sec signals per route, model variant, and region, and surfaces them in a compact heatmap portal. Goal: make regressions visible at deploy time and during canaries by combining synthetic load runs, production-sampled slices, and historical baselines. The output will be a Dashboard + API that query engineers and SREs can use to compare recent runs against baselines, inspect percentile shifts by slice (route/model/region/sequence-length bucket), and produce actionable regression alerts for CI gating and on-call.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry emitter produces p50/p90/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for each (route, model, region, seq_len_bucket) every 1 minute
BenchMesh ingestion pipeline stores run metadata and time-series for at least 90 days
Heatmap portal supports: selected time-range compare, baseline overlay, and click-through to raw traces/requests
Regression detector computes effect size and flags regressions >= 10% p95 increase or 200ms absolute degradation with an adjustable sensitivity knob
CI gating hook allows canary deploy checks to reject rollouts if regression detector fires on canary vs baseline

notes: Implementation will reuse existing percentile-aggregator (see ENG-64999) but extend labels to include model_variant and region-aware buckets.
Plan to retain raw token-level samples for 7 days and aggregated percentiles for 90 days to control storage cost.
Will add a feature flag for CI gating so we can opt into automatic rollback on canary regressions for a few pilot teams.
Alert routing: regressions annotated with affected routes will create a PagerDuty ticket to the inference-oncall by default; lower-severity alerts go to a Slack channel.
